notes: Account: product-led mid-market SaaS providing embedded analytics in B2B apps.
Primary asks: EU data residency, sub-150ms p95 for conversational assistant in EU users, predictable unit costs for embedding-based search.
Initial path: trial Hosted API to validate correctness + latency, then move to Dedicated for data isolation and reserved throughput.
AE call 2025-11-04 (intro): quick product overview, they shared expected QPS ~30-80 with bursts to 200 during peak reports. Cost sensitivity: medium — will pay for predictable SLA if ROI clear.
SE demo 2026-02-18: showed Hosted API latency in eu-west1 region (avg ~90ms, p95 ~180ms at test load), discussed automatic batching and caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
Quote from CTO on call: "We can tolerate some model degradation but cannot send any EU production PII outside region without contract-level guarantee."
Security: asked for SOC2 report, KMS integration options, audit logging retention (1 year min), and SSO (SAML) for console access — drive link with security questionnaire attached.

POC plan agreed 2026-03-10: two-week POC on Dedicated EU-only cluster (eu-west primary, eu-central failover) with synthetic traffic and subset of production prompts; compare Hosted vs Dedicated latency/cost with same model family.
POC success criteria: p95 <150ms on 95% of endpoints, embedding recall delta <2% vs baseline model, cost per 1M tokens within target band in pricing deck.
Pricing convo: they prefer a moderate reserved commit (3-6 months) vs pure on-demand; asked for example ARR scenarios and break-even analysis (linked pricing deck).
Multi-region notes: product team wants EU-primary only; platform team wants ability to failover to us-east in disaster but that triggers data residency concerns — need legal sign-off.

requirements_summary: Workloads: chat-first assistant in-product + search/rerank for KB; batch embeddings for similarity pipelines.
Latency/Throughput: target p95 <150ms for chat API at 50-80 qps sustained; burst handling to 200 qps with graceful degradation.
Model preferences: open/quantized variants preferred (smaller cost footprint), fallback to larger LLMs for complex queries.
Routing/fallback: EU-primary; acceptable to route non-PII to US fallback during bursts only if contract allows; prefer model-variant fallback within EU first.
Security/compliance: EU data residency mandatory, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS for key control, SOC2 certification required
